newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end off worst levels on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end off worst levels on U.S. data.

text.p: South African shares closed off worst levels in fairly active trade, with industrials retracing some losses on U.S. economic data and golds down on a weak bullion price.
Dealers said the jobless claims figures in the U.S. which were largely in line with forecasts pointed to a softening economy and improved sentiment in U.S. bonds.
Rand recovery also boosted sentiment together with some nibbling of stocks at lower levels.
Golds were also helped off worst levels on bargain-hunting but there was concern of bullion breaking below the $380 an ounce level, dealers said.
The overall index fell 14.8 points to 7,008.1 points, industrials lost 7.8 points to 8,252.4 points and golds were off 11.9 points to 1,683.2 points.
